g.text: WS2812 - the protocol engine on both sides
800 kHz single-wire NRZ, 1.25 us cells, 75 clocks exactly
pinned to bit 6, one pad claimed
dmem[11] is RELOADED from dmem[10] every
outer pass - without the reload the inner
counter reads 0, wraps to 255, and the
both paths padded to the same length
if 2 - X == 0 the FRAME IS DONE
watch the WIRE, not the data register
a low longer than 50 us is a RESET,
so the NEXT rising edge is cell 0.
anchoring on the first two rising edges is
the classic TB defect here: for this data
cell k begins at t0 + 75k EXACTLY
the line is sampled at +42 clocks
Why the mask is also the loop counter.
After eight cells the mask has walked 0x80 -> ... -> 0x01 -> 0,
so SHR + JNZ ends the byte with no second counter. A first version kept a
separate 8..1 counter in dmem[3] and the cell came out at 77 clocks - over
budget, because the byte-boundary work had nowhere to hide the extra 3.
Why the byte is not shifted.
This ISA has SHR and no shift-left. "Mask bit 7, then shift the byte right"
reads like MSB-first and is not: after k shifts the bit due at k sits at
7-k, so bit 7 is zero from the second cell and the frame is 24 zeros.
Leaving the byte alone in dmem[6] and walking the mask keeps dmem[0..2] the
frame the firmware was given, in datasheet order.
Why this TB claims equality, not a window.
47 or 49 clocks is 783 or 817 ns and clears every datasheet window in
print. But a cell that is 74 clocks shifts every sample in the frame, and a
byte-boundary path one clock longer stretches three cells in every frame -
a frame 3/24 wrong, which no window check can see and a strip can.
Hence: measured on the PADS, in CLOCKS, requiring t0 + 75k.
